item.title: Taking Fiji Bati to Tier 1 is my goal - Fiji Bati Coach
item.description: Vodafone Fiji Bati coach Mick Potter says he wants the Fiji Bati to become a Tier One nation in rugby league and establish itself among the world's top four teams. Speaking to the media, Potter said he wants to help Fiji return to its winning ways.
item.content:encoded:
Vodafone Fiji Bati coach Mick Potter says he wants the Fiji Bati to become a Tier One nation in rugby league and establish itself among the world's top four teams.

Speaking to the media, Potter said he wants to help Fiji return to its winning ways.

He says it is good to be back with the Fiji Bati coaching staff and, with 77 days to go before the Rugby League World Cup, he is looking forward to the challenge ahead.

Potter says he is passionate about his new role and excited about the team's preparations for the World Cup.

Insert Potter making statements 30th July

The Fiji Bati is in the same pool as Australia, New Zealand and the Cook Islands for the Rugby League World Cup, which kicks off in October.

item.title: Home advantage gives Rewa boost in OFC Men’s Champions League
item.description: Rewa FC will carry Fiji's hopes in the OFC Men's Champions League as the Delta Tigers prepare to represent the country on home soil, with Fiji Football Association CEO Mohammed Yusuf saying hosting the tournament gives them a major advantage. item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC will carry Fiji's hopes in the OFC Men's Champions League as the Delta Tigers prepare to represent the country on home soil, with Fiji Football Association CEO Mohammed Yusuf saying hosting the tournament gives them a major advantage.

Yusuf says Fiji Football decided to bid to host the competition after opportunities were opened for member associations to stage OFC tournaments, knowing a Fijian club would qualify.

He says the Association will invest about $120,000 to host the tournament, believing the home advantage gives Rewa its best chance of challenging for the title.

Rewa has also received financial assistance from Fiji Football Association, along with the opportunity to use the Fiji FA Academy as the team’s training base in the lead-up to the tournament.

He says Rewa will have the opportunity to play at home against some of Oceania's top clubs, including defending champions Auckland City and teams from Tahiti, New Caledonia, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, Papua New Guinea and the Cook Islands.

Yusuf says the investment is worthwhile as Fijian clubs have previously travelled to Tahiti, Vanuatu and Honiara but have fallen short of reaching the final.

He says Suva reached the semi-finals in Vanuatu, while Rewa also made the semi-finals in Tahiti.

He says Rewa has been the most consistent team in 2025 after winning the Extra Premier League and the FMF Inter District Championship, while maintaining their standard this season despite several players moving to Bula FC.

This will be the club's third consecutive appearance in the OFC Men's Champions League following campaigns in Tahiti and Honiara.

He also confirms Fiji Football has secured the hosting rights for the 2027 OFC Men's Champions League, meaning the 2027 Extra Premier League champions will also have the opportunity to compete on home soil.

Fiji Football Association President Rajesh Patel says although hosting the tournament has placed a financial burden on the Association, it is worthwhile because Rewa is representing Fiji, and Fiji Football is committed to providing every possible form of assistance.

Patel says winning the OFC Men’s Champions League would see Rewa qualify for what he referred to as the FIFA Club Championship, giving the club the opportunity to compete on the world stage.

Meanwhile, Rewa FC Senior Vice President Sunjay Patel thanks Fiji Football for its financial assistance and for allowing the team to use the Fiji FA Academy as its training base in the lead-up to the tournament.

He says finding suitable training grounds in Fiji is challenging, making the support invaluable.

The Senior Vice President also acknowledges Fiji Football's support for Rewa's Red Kachi Kachi youth development programme, which now has 218 children aged between six and 14 participating, with footballs also being provided through Fiji Football's partnership with McDonald's.

He says winning the OFC Men’s Champions League would be Rewa's biggest achievement and has called on all Fijians to get behind the team as it aims to bring the title home.

The OFC Men’s Champions League kicks off on August 9th, with Rewa opening its campaign against Vanuatu's Galaxy FC at Churchill Park in Lautoka at 3pm.

The remaining group matches, as well as the semi-finals and final, will be played at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.

item.title: Southern Zone ready to take on the east - Wadali
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 30/07/2026 President of the Vodafone Deans Southern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby Association, Rusiate Wadali, says Southern Zone teams are well prepared to take on their Eastern Zone counterparts in this weekend's Under-18 elimination round.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 30/07/2026

President of the Vodafone Deans Southern Zone Secondary Schools Rugby Association, Rusiate Wadali, says Southern Zone teams are well prepared to take on their Eastern Zone counterparts in this weekend's Under-18 elimination round.

Marist Brothers High School and Ratu Sukuna Memorial School will travel to St Vincent Ground, where they will face Lelean Memorial School and Ratu Kadavulevu School respectively.

Wadali says although the matches will be played in the East, coaches have been urged to step up their preparations to ensure the players are ready.

He says the Southern Zone has the highest number of teams that qualified for the national eliminations and they are ready to take on the challenge.

Insert: Wadali on South ready – 30 July 2026

The Under-18 elimination matches will be played at four venues this Saturday: St Vincent Ground in Tailevu, Grammar Ground in Suva, Lawaqa Park in Sigatoka and Ratu Ganilau Park in Savusavu.

At St Vincent Ground, Lelean Memorial School will face Marist Brothers High School at 12.20pm, while Ratu Kadavulevu School will take on Ratu Sukuna Memorial School at 1.50pm.

At Grammar Ground, Nasinu Secondary School will play Holy Cross College at 12.20pm, while Suva Grammar School will meet Ratu Luke Secondary School.

Meanwhile, Queen Victoria School will travel to Lawaqa Park to face Ba Provincial Free Bird Institute at 10am, while Cuvu College will take on St John's College at 1pm.

At Ratu Ganilau Park, Ratu Navula College will face Shiri Guru Nanak Khalsa College at 2pm, before Ra High School meets Navatu Secondary School at 3.25pm.

item.title: Fijian-born Cikamatana sets Commonwealth Games record to win third straight gold
item.description: Fijian born Australian weightlifter Eileen Cikamatana has set a new 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games record on her way to winning gold in the Women's 86kg division. Cikamatana lifted 108kg in the Snatch and 140kg in the Clean & Jerk for a combined lift of 248kg.
item.content:encoded:
Fijian born Australian weightlifter Eileen Cikamatana has set a new 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games record on her way to winning gold in the Women's 86kg division.

Cikamatana lifted 108kg in the Snatch and 140kg in the Clean & Jerk for a combined lift of 248kg.

She is the third female weightlifter in history to achieve the Commonwealth Games feat of three titles in a row, joining India's Mirabai Chanu (women's 48kg) and Canadian weightlifter Maude Charron (63kg) after they also won gold in Glasgow.

Cikamatana has dominated her weightlifting categories since winning gold for Fiji in the 90kg event at the 2018 Gold Coast Games.

She then switched allegiance to Australia the following year due to a local dispute with Fiji's weightlifting governing body, and to keep working with coach Paul Coffa.

Taking out the 87kg title at the 2022 Birmingham edition, Cikamatana is also the first woman to win Commonwealth Games gold for two countries in an individual sport.

item.title: 2026/2027 HSBC SVNS World Series calendar confirmed
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 30/07/2026 The 2026/2027 HSBC SVNS World Series will once again visit Dubai, Cape Town, Singapore, Perth, Vancouver and New York before culminating in the HSBC SVNS World Championship, which will be held across Hong Kong, Valladolid and Bordeaux.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 30/07/2026

The 2026/2027 HSBC SVNS World Series will once again visit Dubai, Cape Town, Singapore, Perth, Vancouver and New York before culminating in the HSBC SVNS World Championship, which will be held across Hong Kong, Valladolid and Bordeaux.

The Dubai 7s will kick off the series on the 28th and 29th of November this year, followed by the Cape Town 7s on the 5th and 6th of December.

The Singapore 7s will be played on the 30th and 31st of January 2027, followed by the Perth 7s on the 6th and 7th of February, the Vancouver 7s on the 6th and 7th of March, and the New York 7s on the 13th and 14th of March.

The SVNS World Championship will begin with the Hong Kong 7s from the 9th to the 11th of April, followed by the Valladolid 7s from the 21st to the 23rd of May, before concluding in Bordeaux from the 28th to the 30th of May.

The Fiji Airways Fiji men's 7s team finished second in the 2025/2026 SVNS World Series, while the Fijiana 7s side placed sixth.

At the SVNS World Championship, the men's team finished sixth, while the Fijiana 7s team placed seventh.

item.title: Emily Sanatan through after penalty shootout win over Abua
item.description: Mohammed Feroz , Nilufa Buksh · 30/07/2026 Emily Sanatan booked their place in the next round of the CKS Mega Bargain Labasa Sanatan Tournament after defeating Abua Sanatan in a dramatic penalty shootout in front of thousands of football fans who packed Subrail Park to watch Fiji international Roy Krishna.
item.content:encoded:
Mohammed Feroz , Nilufa Buksh · 30/07/2026

Emily Sanatan booked their place in the next round of the CKS Mega Bargain Labasa Sanatan Tournament after defeating Abua Sanatan in a dramatic penalty shootout in front of thousands of football fans who packed Subrail Park to watch Fiji international Roy Krishna.

The electric atmosphere reached its peak during the tournament's final knockout fixture, as supporters stayed until the final whistle to watch Roy Krishna and Emily Sanatan battle Abua Sanatan in a fiercely contested encounter.

Both teams produced an entertaining display of football, showcasing impressive skill, determination and teamwork throughout the match.

Emily Sanatan struck first when a dangerous free kick into the penalty area was brilliantly headed into the back of the net to give them the early advantage.

Abua Sanatan responded strongly and piled on the pressure after falling behind.

Their persistence paid off when a powerful free kick took a deflection off an Emily defender before finding the back of the net for an own goal, bringing the scores level at 1-1.

Emily created several chances to regain the lead, but Roy Krishna was closely marked by the Abua defence, preventing the Fiji star from getting on the scoresheet.

With neither side able to find a winner in regulation time, the match went to a penalty shootout, where Emily Sanatan held their nerve to defeat Abua Sanatan and secure their place in the next stage.

Abua's task became even more difficult after one of their midfielders was shown a red card, reducing the side to ten players.

Speaking to fijivillage Sports Krishna says it was a tough encounter, adding that every match becomes more challenging once teams reach the knockout stages.

Krishna also expresses his gratitude to the thousands of fans who turned out to support the match and encouraged football supporters to continue coming out in large numbers to support the Labasa Sanatan Tournament.

item.title: Konataci finishes in 9th place in men's discus with seasonal best
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 30/07/2026 Team Fiji athlete Sitiveni Konataci finished ninth in the men's discus throw F42-44/F61-64 final this morning at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Scotland.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 30/07/2026

Team Fiji athlete Sitiveni Konataci finished ninth in the men's discus throw F42-44/F61-64 final this morning at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Scotland.

Konataci recorded a season's best throw of 27.54 metres.

In other results, Yeshnil Karan finished 12th in the One Mile heats, Kelera Mudunasoko placed fifth in the women's 200 metres breaststroke heats, and Jasmine Daunakamakama advanced to the semi-finals of the women's 57kg division with a commanding 4-1 victory over Sri Lanka's Keshani Hansika.

Later tonight, Elizabeth Moceiwai will resume her women's singles sectional campaign at 7.30pm, before Fiji's men's pairs bowling team returns to action in its sectional match at 8.55pm.

In weightlifting, Taniela Tuisuva Rainibogi will compete in the men's 110kg event, which gets underway at 8.30pm tonight.

Meanwhile, Australia continues to lead the medal tally with 47 gold, 21 silver and 35 bronze medals. Canada is second with 14 gold, 11 silver and 14 bronze medals, while England sits third with 12 gold, 27 silver and 17 bronze medals.
